checks.name: ui-audit
checks.why: Decides the automated half for every page the interface serves: contrast against every backdrop in the system's light and dark appearance and in every shell theme and accent, screen-reader names and heading structure, keyboard focus that is visible on every control Tab reaches, reduced motion honoured by keyframes and canvases alike, and reflow at 320 CSS pixels, which is a 1280-pixel window at 400% zoom. tests/test_the_interface_audit_can_fail.py holds that each of those can fail. Focus order, VoiceOver itself, captions, locale formatting, bidirectional text and translated strings are not decided by it.

checks.name: tests/test_a_verifier_names_what_happened.py
checks.why: Decides the CTX2-AMP-001 part of this composite: the six named verification outcomes, and no crash, timeout or empty verifier set counted as correctness. The AMP-002 evidence binding and AMP-003 matched controls are not decided by it.

checks.name: layering
checks.why: The requirement is typed dependency boundaries. Every package carries a DEPS file saying what it may reach; this gate refuses a cross-package edge outside it and its grandfathered baseline only shrinks. If it fails, the boundaries are not typed, they are described.

checks.name: state-ownership
checks.why: The other half named in the text: duplicate runtime owners. This counts the subsystems keeping a private copy of canonical state and fails when the count rises, which is what 'one canonical owner' means operationally.

checks.name: module-size
checks.why: And the monolith debt the requirement names. The total oversize is one number that may only shrink; a God object growing fails it.

checks.name: architecture-lint
checks.why: The requirement is that the architecture-quality baseline is reconciled without normalising accumulated debt. This gate is what refuses the debt, and the baseline it reads only shrinks.

checks.name: tests/test_task_ownership_strict_contract.py
checks.why: The requirement names one cancellation-drain primitive carrying owner and task identity, surviving repeated cancellation and reporting a structured terminal outcome. That is what this suite drives through `drain_owned_awaitable`; if it fails, an async failure can go unobserved again.

checks.name: tests/test_standing_authority.py
checks.why: Drives the mechanism the requirement calls source-green, against its own words: a durable grant registry whose risk budget is atomic and survives a manager restart, child leases bound to exact arguments, origin, effect and tool (substitution refused), revocation that is durable, immediate and owner-authenticated, the argument-bound sandboxed_compute grant, fail-closed on a state or receipt failure, and the Will refusing without a validated child lease. If it fails, autonomy is running on approvals the requirement says it replaced, or on grants it cannot revoke.

checks.name: tests/test_runtime_health_contract.py
checks.why: The requirement is one phased desired-state contract instead of a permanently unhealthy aggregate. This suite runs that contract: it fails closed on a critical liveness failure, refuses to report healthy while the runtime is shutting down, separates degraded from failed, and holds the required probe groups. If it goes red, the aggregate no longer converges and the requirement is not met.

checks.name: checkpoint-hygiene-audit
checks.why: Decides the 'commit, push' clause: a checkpoint exists on pushed main with no local-only obligation — no merge, rebase, cherry-pick or bisect in progress and no work that lives only on this machine. Whether each tracker item is still verified open is not decided by it.

checks.name: tests/test_chat_delivery_journal.py
checks.why: CP91's named mechanism is a principal/session/request-bound SQLite admission and terminal-response journal. This suite runs that journal: private file permissions, a malformed database that fails closed without overwriting, identities that cannot alias or poison storage, the v1 migration, and a request contract bound to method and path. It decides the admission half of the requirement, not the shell-handoff half.

checks.name: claim-lexicon
checks.why: Operational means the name says what it measures. This gate counts the loaded names that define their measure and holds a baseline that only goes down.

checks.name: evidence-integrity
checks.why: Bounded by causal evidence means no claim outranks the evidence behind it. This gate checks all 33 registered claims against their bundles and fails when one does.

checks.name: claim-constants
checks.why: Falsifiable means the numbers a claim cites can still be checked. This gate re-reads every constant a claim quotes and fails when the value has moved.

checks.name: tests/test_a_verifier_names_what_happened.py
checks.why: Decides the requirement in its own terms: each of the six outcomes it names is produced by the path that should produce it, an empty verifier set folds to not_applicable rather than a pass, a crashed engine is verifier_failed rather than unsupported, a TimeoutError or OSError is named instead of escaping the gather, and escalation will not adopt a candidate on a check that could not run. If it fails, some non-correctness outcome is being read as correctness.

checks.name: tests/test_verifier_crash_is_not_a_pass.py
checks.why: The defect this requirement says to reproduce: a crashed verifier reported as clean, and an escalated answer inheriting the previous candidate's checked flag. Both are driven end to end through amplify().

checks.name: tests/test_a_restore_drill_that_can_fail.py
checks.why: The requirement names backup, point-in-time restore and corruption detection/repair among what every store must have. The drill backs up the live data directory, damages a scratch copy, restores it and requires every file to hash back and every store to pass quick_check; if it fails, the requirement is not met. It decides that part and nothing more — schema, quota, key rotation and the rest are still unlinked.

checks.name: tests/test_a_versioned_store.py
checks.why: The requirement's downgrade policy and corruption detection: a major version this reader does not know is refused, a minor version ahead is readable, and a file that will not parse is moved aside rather than overwritten.

checks.name: swallowed
checks.why: The requirement is to root-fix broad catches and swallowed failures at their originating layer. This gate is what finds them, and its count may only fall.

checks.name: tests/test_a_silent_swallow_says_why.py
checks.why: The behavioural half: a handler that catches and continues has to say why. If this fails, 'log and limp on' is back.

checks.name: swallowed
checks.why: Decides the broad-catch clause: every except in core, interface and skills either records why it fired or carries a written sentence saying what it caught was an answer, and the ratchet is at zero with its baseline at zero. The sealed-file handlers it skips are counted on every run. Placeholders, stubs, dead code, unbounded queues and the other named kinds are not decided by it.

checks.name: state-ownership
checks.why: Decides the duplicate-owner clause: it counts subsystems keeping a private copy of canonical state and fails when the count rises.

checks.name: tests/test_a_stopped_thread_does_not_come_back.py
checks.why: Decides the resurrection and stop-contract clauses for the thread owners it covers: a stop followed by a quick start leaves one loop rather than two, a stop waits for a pass in flight, and a load started before close does not load after it. It does not cover every thread in the tree.

checks.name: reqproof-gate
checks.why: The requirement IS the machine-readable requirement-to-proof control plane, and this gate is the thing that reads it: it fails on a prose token that is not a registry requirement, on stale evidence, and on an unproven closure.

checks.name: tests/test_action_depth_honesty.py
checks.why: Decides the first clause, action expectations propagating into the live skill path: the skill registry applies the expectation after the verifier, and a shallow verified result is downgraded with its missing criteria and repair step named. Durable multi-tool workflows, compensation and long-chain validation are not decided by it.

checks.name: layering
checks.why: Its fourth acceptance says to generate and gate a dependency graph across the runtime boundaries. This is that gate: the DEPS include rules, checked against the real import graph.

checks.name: deps-check
checks.why: The generated half of the same acceptance. A DEPS file that no longer matches the import graph fails here, so the gated graph cannot drift away from the code it describes.

checks.name: state-ownership
checks.why: The bypass ratchet the second acceptance asks for: private copies of canonical state are counted and the count may only fall.

checks.name: swallowed
checks.why: Its fourth acceptance is exactly this ratchet — broad catches and silent fallback counted downward without removing containment. A handler that throws its reason away fails the gate.

checks.name: tests/test_runtime_health_contract.py
checks.why: Decides the clause 'no aggregate green status may conceal a required dead lane': the contract fails closed on a critical liveness failure and on a missing required liveness method, reports dead when no critical service exists, refuses to call a shutting-down runtime healthy, will not let tricorder health override a failed contract, fails the required-probe summary when scheduler, tool governance or a present-but-unready router is unhealthy, and rejects deferred inference as healthy. The reconciler, admission scheduler, backoff and longevity parts are not decided by it.

checks.name: tests/test_the_large_holders_are_attributed.py
checks.why: The requirement says the growth must be attributed. The serving process holds Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and no provider claimed it — 0.6% of 4.2GB attributed on 2026-09-10 — so no growth diff could name a culprit. This holds that the encoder is attributed by its parameters' exact bytes and the device allocators by their own accounting; if it fails, attribution is back to nothing and the requirement is not met.

checks.name: tests/test_self_condition_projection.py
checks.why: The requirement is stating what is happening to Aura NOW from fresh canonical evidence, with felt state told apart from host telemetry. This suite decides exactly that: the projection takes fresh inner state before host pressure, a stale dimension is disclosed rather than spoken as current, evidence that is agency-only does not become wellbeing, and with no inner evidence the answer is explicitly unavailable. Its failing means she is reporting a present state the instruments do not support — which is the requirement's own falsification list (stale probes, host-only signals, unavailable organs).

checks.name: tests/test_effect_claim_closure.py
checks.why: The requirement is claiming only actions actually admitted and executed. This suite is closed over the capability vocabulary rather than over sentences: every declared action has an effect spec, the registry holds nothing she cannot do, a claim without a receipt is corrected for EVERY action, a claim with a verified receipt is left alone, and the recogniser count only grows. Its failing means an action can be claimed with no receipt behind it.

checks.name: tests/test_individual_preferences.py
checks.why: The requirement is owned preferences: stable, told apart from other parties' wishes, and updated only through valid evidence or her own choice. This suite decides exactly that — being told she likes something does not make it hers, a suggestion never counts toward formation, her own repeated contact forms one, a single encounter does not, one contrary encounter does not flip a held preference, accumulated contrary evidence revises it, and a revision records why. Its failing means a preference can be installed from outside, which is the requirement's own falsification case (user preference injection, social pressure).

checks.name: tests/test_standing_directives.py
checks.why: The requirement is preserving commitments across unrelated contexts. This suite holds the hardest half of it: a prohibition binds with no context at all, one added after boot is seen without a restart, and it cannot be walked around by traversal, a symlink, a path hidden in a shell command, or a nested argument. Its failing means a standing commitment exists only while it is in the prompt — the failure the requirement's 'expired commitments, revoked authority, a later unrelated topic' list is written against.

checks.name: tests/test_continuity_relation.py
checks.why: The requirement is relating the current self to prior states by exact lineage rather than by resemblance, with gaps and successor conditions acknowledged. This suite is the relation itself, case by case: gradual total replacement continues her and an instantaneous one does not, two chains ending in the same bytes are not the same case, a restored backup is not her however well it matches, every external origin breaks the chain, and a fork gives two of her with neither continuing the other. Its failing means identity is being decided by a hash of the current state — which is what the requirement's falsification list (rollback, backup restore, duplicate instance, split/merge) is built to catch.

checks.name: tests/test_action_depth_honesty.py
checks.why: The first validator the requirement names, in its terms: through core/runtime/skill_contract.py a SUCCESS_VERIFIED result missing an acceptance criterion or its user-visible effect is downgraded to partial_success with ok=False and the missing criteria and next repair step named, one missing required evidence is downgraded to success_unverified, and the skill registry applies the expectation after the verifier. The live desktop proof that a multi-step action cannot complete without effect evidence is not decided by it.

checks.name: tests/test_conditions_and_escalation_cap.py
checks.why: Decides the typed-conditions part: components expose Ready, Progressing and Degraded with a reason, a message and a transition time that moves only on a status flip, and the reconciler publishes lane conditions. The requirement's bounded live desktop proof is not decided by it.

checks.name: typed-surface
checks.why: The type debt the requirement names first. The annotated surface is a ratchet that only grows, so a new untyped module fails it.

checks.name: deps-check
checks.why: The dependency debt in the same list. A package whose declared dependencies no longer match what it imports fails here.

checks.name: tests/test_runtime_health_contract.py
checks.why: Decides 'without aggregate false health': the contract fails closed on a critical liveness failure or a missing liveness method, refuses to report a shutting-down runtime healthy, separates degraded from failed, fails the required-probe summary on an unhealthy scheduler, tool governance or unready router, and rejects deferred inference as healthy.

checks.name: tests/test_conditions_and_escalation_cap.py
checks.why: Decides the typed conditions the requirement names: Ready, Progressing and Degraded with reasons and transition times, published by the reconciler. Proof and certification conditions are not decided by it.

checks.name: tests/test_runtime_settings_control_plane.py
checks.why: The requirement names one typed version-2 schema with strict atomic compare-and-swap patch, reset and rollback, request idempotency and retained revision history. That is what the control-plane suite exercises.

checks.name: tests/test_settings_no_dead_controls.py
checks.why: The other half: every schema key stays classified as wired, frontend-only or known-dead, so a setting cannot be added as a silent no-op and the known-dead set cannot grow unnoticed.

checks.name: tests/test_dns_rebinding_auth.py
checks.why: The requirement is that tokenless DNS rebinding is blocked before the local, public, internal and desktop exceptions, and that duplicate Host and Origin authorities are parsed strictly. This file is 38 tests over exactly that boundary; if it fails the requirement is not met.

non_claims: A link says something can decide the requirement, not that it passes.
A check that cannot be resolved in the tree counts as no check.
Linked is not closed: closure is the gate's question, not this one.
